title: Preparing for Interviews
summary: Learn how to prepare for an interview by researching the opportunity, reviewing your own experience, planning examples, preparing questions, and getting ready to communicate clearly.
objectives: Identify information to research before an interview.
Prepare relevant examples from personal experience.
Develop thoughtful questions to ask an interviewer.

vocab.def: A structured conversation used to evaluate fit, qualifications, interests, experience, and expectations.
Researching the role and organization and preparing relevant examples, questions, and logistics.
A question asking for an example of how you handled a past situation.
A question used to clarify or explore an answer in more detail.

sections.heading: Research before the conversation
sections.body: Review the organization, role, duties, location, schedule, requirements, and other available information. Preparation helps you ask better questions and explain why the opportunity interests you.

sections.heading: Know your own examples
sections.body: Review projects, school activities, work, volunteering, teamwork, challenges, accomplishments, and mistakes that could help explain how you approach responsibilities.

sections.heading: Prepare for more than perfect-success stories
sections.body: Interviewers may ask about problems, disagreements, mistakes, unfamiliar tasks, priorities, or feedback. A useful answer can show what happened, what you did, and what you learned.

sections.heading: Interviews work both ways
sections.body: Candidates can also ask respectful questions about responsibilities, training, supervision, schedule, expectations, team structure, workplace conditions, and next steps.

practice.prompt: You are interviewing for a role that emphasizes teamwork. What should you prepare?
practice.answer: A truthful example showing your role on a team, what you contributed, how you communicated, and what happened.

practice.prompt: Why should you prepare questions for an employer?
practice.answer: Questions help you understand the opportunity and show that you have thought seriously about the role and expectations.

quiz.question: Which is the strongest interview-preparation strategy?
options: Research the opportunity and prepare truthful examples relevant to its requirements
Memorize one answer for every possible question
Avoid learning anything about the organization
quiz.answer: Research the opportunity and prepare truthful examples relevant to its requirements

lab.objective: Prepare for a simulated interview by reviewing a job description, selecting three relevant experience examples, and writing five questions to ask the interviewer.

reflectionPrompt: Which experience would you want ready if an interviewer asked you to describe a challenge you handled responsibly?
